units.translation: symbols: the agreements which cities, having made with each other, prescribe for their citizens, so as to give and receive what is just
what vengeance will stop the tears of the fatherland?
with the mattock of Zeus who brings justice
light of a day that brings justice
do you mean a judge or an avenger?
(as διπλῆ ὀσφῦς [double loins] in Pollux 1, 190 and spina duplex [double spine] in Vergil) M. Schmidt.
for διπλάσιον [double] perhaps δίκρουν [forked] should be restored: see under διπλάσιος [double].
double vision or double. Aeschylus in Nurses (fr. 47).
you will be entangled in an endless net of ruin
you cast a covering net over the towers of Troy
he is wounded; to speak of the net is more than enough
was the title of a play of Aeschylus, about which see the note on Fragm. p. 103.
Wrongly Δικτυουργοί [Net-Workers] in the old catalogue of plays.
where the meter requires δίμορα τέλεα [twofold complete things], which Hermann restored.
Schol.: ήδέως ἔχω τὸ δίμοιρον τῶν κακῶν σὺν ἑνὶ ἀγαθῷ, ὅ ἐστι τῇ ἀπαλλαγῇ τοῦ γάμου [I gladly accept the two-thirds share of evils with one good, which is the release from marriage].
I praise the better part of evil and the two-thirds share
I gladly accept the two-thirds share of evils with one good, which is the release from marriage
he whirls the horses, raging in their headbands
I shuddered at the great threshing floor, I mean the circle of the shield, as he whirled it
in the hard whirlpools of necessity
with just and fulfilling thoughts, a heart whirled in circles
in the midst of a hard-fought whirlpool
and you, O Zeus-born warlike might, become the city-saving Pallas
at the very tomb of Zeus-born Amphion
and the passages of the heavenly stars
a blast from Zeus, producing fear, advances openly
may a holy end, accomplished by war, come from Zeus
of the double-throned and double-sceptered honor from Zeus
for the thunderbolt from Zeus is hurled at the eyes
to end in this way from Zeus
to declare these just powers from Zeus
[or Suppl. 155 corruptly for ἡλιόκτυπον [struck by the sun], which see]
and the remaining army perished in the land of the Boeotians
you perished by the bolt-fastened spear
for the royal power has perished utterly
which is said by tmesis for μεταδιόμεναι [pursuing after]. It is a Homeric verb, about which see Hermann's note on Pers. 701.
